title: EXPO / City Pavilion
techniques: Nine-part thin-instanced human figures with animated limbs and aisle graph motion
Dijkstra destination routing over obstacle-checked aisle edges with corner-facility detours
Day/night illumination, real-time PCF shadows, emissive windows and HDR bloom
Projected readable destination labels, furnished exhibits, 32-building city and animated traffic
limitations: Crowd motion and matrix animation are CPU driven; people may overlap one another
Wall-frame timings are not GPU timestamp measurements
Projected labels use screen-space UI; overhead map is near-vertical perspective
One fixed 2048px directional shadow map; hall point lights do not cast additional shadows
Quick tunnel is temporary and requires persistent local processes
testSummary: Production build passed. Isolated Chrome at 1440x960 CSS and DPR 2 verified native WebGPU and forced WebGL2, 2880x1920 backing at default 120 and maximum 1,200 people, fixed 100% with adaptive OFF. Manual 50% produced 1440x960. All 30 destinations reachable with obstacle-free routes; blocked crowd edges: 0. Day/night, overhead map, orbit/pan/zoom, projected-label selection, pause, 24-person minimum and walking animation passed. Original scene default/max native HiDPI also passed. No console/page errors. Both scenes passed live resize and DPR-change checks. Evidence: artifacts/exhibition-tests.json and artifacts/hidpi-label-tests.json. Static production artifacts passed under /eval-gpu/babylon/: both scene links, native WebGPU and forced WebGL2, native DPR 2 at default/max, route/night controls, all assets including compiler WASM inside prefix, zero request/HTTP/console/page errors.
